source: Actual Literate extension playback, Kokoro Heart (af_heart), recorded locally through Chrome tab audio
processing: Leading/trailing recording silence trimmed. One silent buffering pause shortened from the measured gap to 0.550 seconds; no spoken words removed or tempo change. Two-pass FFmpeg loudnorm targeting -19 LUFS and -1.5 dBTP, 48 kHz mono PCM16. Tail padding/trim holds the exact edited sample count. Raw, full unedited trimmed master, and silence-edited master are preserved.

chapters.text: Literate is a free, open-source extension built to read to you. It works with articles, selected text, and local PDFs.

Instant voice mode uses voices already installed on your device and can start almost immediately, even on slower devices, though some voices may sound robotic. Natural voice mode uses a downloaded Kokoro model for more natural narration, but may need time to warm up before playback. Its files stay cached for later reading.
On an article, you can listen to the main text with words highlighted as it plays. Selected passages also have a right-click option: Read selection aloud.
The section picker lets you focus on a particular part of the page, leaving sidebars and related stories outside the reading area.
The mini player keeps scrolling text nearby. You can click individual words to jump around, or pin the player above other windows in supported browsers.
You can customize the narration speed and the extension’s appearance, with light and dark modes and a choice of accent colors. Periwinkle is the default.
Local PDFs are supported with Chrome’s file-access permission. The reader works with existing text, while scanned documents need text recognition first.
The speech runs on your device. Kokoro’s files download from Hugging Face, and the source page needs to remain open while the mini player is in use.

captionTiming: Film-relative; includes the 1.5-second narration placement offset.
cueTimingBasis: Local cached tiny.en ASR word alignment to canonical narration, with word starts corrected against measured leading/paragraph quiet spans. Approximate phonetic onsets; no canonical words omitted. All cues after the one silent cut subtract its exact removed-sample duration.

silenceEdits.mapping: Before sourceStart: unchanged; after sourceEnd: subtract removedSeconds; no spoken samples removed.
